headline.text: Keski-Uusimaa lags nationally in crude MDT recording at 0.0% (95% CI 0.0–0.8) versus 6.0%, while crude curative treatment is 33.7% (95% CI 29.6–38.0) versus 27.0%.

details.text: In Keski-Uusimaa, the crude recorded MDT meeting share is 0.0% (95% CI 0.0–0.8; n=0/481) compared with 6.0% (893/14873) nationally; the 95% confidence interval excludes the national value, though HILMO entries come only from direct patient contacts and measure recording practice, not care.

Across overlapping treatment categories where a patient can have several treatments, Keski-Uusimaa's crude curative share is 33.7% (95% CI 29.6–38.0; n=162/481) versus 27.0% (4009/14873) nationally, and its 95% confidence interval excludes the national value.

The county's crude life-prolonging treatment share is 28.9% (95% CI 25.0–33.1; n=139/481) versus 30.4% (4522/14873) nationally, and its crude symptomatic treatment share is 39.5% (95% CI 35.2–43.9; n=190/481) versus 39.5% (5871/14873) nationally; their 95% confidence intervals include the national values.

Public data do not measure county waiting times, while preliminary, unpublished national figures average 155 days from symptoms to treatment in Finland versus 107 days in Sweden and 67 days in Denmark, with 56 days of patient delay, 41 days in primary care, and 58 days in specialist care.

headline.text: Keski-Uusimaa's crude 26.4% (95% CI 22.7–30.5) no-treatment-record share versus 27.5% nationally suggests relatively complete treatment recording, but county shares lack age and stage adjustment and pathway timestamps.

details.text: The crude share with no treatment record within 12 months is 26.4% (95% CI 22.7–30.5; n=127/481) versus 27.5% (4089/14873) nationally, with the 95% confidence interval including 27.5%; this mixes untreated patients and treatment that was not recorded, and as an inference, a data-quality signal below 27.5% is consistent with relatively complete treatment recording, not direct evidence.

County shares are crude and not adjusted for age or stage; stage at diagnosis is missing for a large share of new patients nationally, and while Kuva 16 provides digitised national age-adjusted curative reference lines of 26.7% for men and 26.9% for women (±0.5 percentage points precision), no county age-adjusted figure is available here.

A journal article reports that HILMO hospital discharge diagnoses match the Cancer Registry for about 90% of most cancer types, but this concerns diagnosis concordance only and says nothing about how completely treatment, referrals, or MDT meetings are recorded.

Public report data do not measure symptom onset or referrals, primary care visits are not included in the report's data and occupational health is not mentioned, imaging appears only indirectly as the diagnostic basis in approximately 20% of cases nationally, and specialist visits and treatments lack county waiting-time timestamps.

headline.text: The team recommends publishing county recording completeness for MDT, stage, and drug treatment, reporting access times using THL 21/2016 definitions, and standardising referrals and diagnostic coordination.

details.text: Given Keski-Uusimaa's crude recorded MDT share of 0.0% (95% CI 0.0–0.8; n=0/481) versus 6.0% (893/14873) nationally and incomplete national stage and lung cancer data, the team recommends publishing county recording completeness for stage, drug treatment, and MDT coding while reading gaps as data-quality signals, as the roadmap plans a quality registry with 90% coverage including stage.

Because the Health Care Act sets no legal maximum time for a cancer suspicion, the team recommends reporting access times using THL guidance Ohjaus 21/2016 definitions for 16 cancers and flagging stalled handovers, while the roadmap plans national target access times in 2026–2028 and the Filha programme's diagnostics guideline is due before the 2030 interim evaluation.

Because referral instructions vary by county and mentor insight notes that weak referrals receive lower urgency ratings in specialist care, the team recommends a standard referral template, pulmonologist referral for persistent symptoms despite a normal X-ray, and a named diagnostic-phase contact person, while the roadmap plans standardised referral criteria and care-coordinator guidance in 2026–2028.

rec:1.claim_text: Team recommendation 1: Counties report access times using the THL 21/2016 definitions, with handover alerts. Each wellbeing services county reports lung cancer access times (referral → first specialist visit → diagnosis → treatment start) using the definitions in THL's Hoitoonpääsyn seuranta syövän hoidossa (Ohjaus 21/2016). Until national target times exist, flag stalled handovers.
rec:1.location: §1. Counties report access times using the THL 21/2016 definitions, with handover alerts

rec:2.claim_text: Team recommendation 2: A KYS-style referral template, a persistent-symptoms rule and a named contact. Adopt a standard referral content list and template, modelled on KYS. • Add a rule for primary care: if symptoms persist after a normal X-ray, refer for a pulmonologist assessment. • Name a contact person for the diagnostic phase, from referral to diagnosis.
rec:2.location: §2. A KYS-style referral template, a persistent-symptoms rule and a named contact

rec:3.claim_text: Team recommendation 3: Report recording completeness per county: stage, drug treatment, MDT coding. Publish, per county, how completely stage, drug treatment and MDT meetings are recorded. Read county ‘gaps’ in these fields as data-quality signals first.
rec:3.location: §3. Report recording completeness per county: stage, drug treatment, MDT coding
